newsitem.title: ITALY: Olivetti shares open up but fade fast.
newsitem.headline: Olivetti shares open up but fade fast.

text.p: Shares in Italian information technology group Olivetti opened nearly four percent up on the Milan bourse on Thursday, after it announced a pre-tax loss for 1996, but faded quickly as the session wore on.

Olivetti gave preliminary 1996 results after the market closed on Wednesday, saying its pre-tax loss would be around 800 billion lire ($497 million) while annual sales slumped 16 percent to 8.27 trillion lire from levels seen in 1995.

The stock, which had been penalised before the provisional results were released, had an opening price of 677 lire per share, up 3.99 percent on the day. By 0910 GMT it was trading only 1.08 percent higher at 658 lire.

"The fall of the last few days has skimmed the speculation off the market and the figures are in line with forecasts, but they're not talking about a capital increase," one broker said shortly after the start.

The market judged a fall in the financial requirement to 2.25 trillion lire from 2.916 trillion lire at the end of November, and more than three trillion at the end of August, as positive but was concerned about the drop in sales.
CIR and Cofide, family holdings of former Olivetti chairman Carlo De Benedetti, were moving in opposite directions on the firmer bourse.
CIR was 2.94 percent stronger at 1190 lire per ordinary share while Cofide was 1.23 percent lower at 741 lire.
